# tree-sitter-haskell 0.23.1, vendored by pmacs

The crate as published to crates.io (from tree-sitter/tree-sitter-haskell at
`c30d812bc90827f1a54106a25bc9a6307f5cdcec`, recorded in `.cargo_vcs_info.json`),
with the upstream `LICENSE` from that commit added, since the published crate
carries none, and one change: `src/tree_sitter/array.h` is tree-sitter-rust
0.24.2's, the header tree-sitter's CLI has generated since 0.24 (the same bytes
as `vendor/tree-sitter-python`'s and `vendor/tree-sitter-yaml`'s). Its
`array_push` assigns `contents` from the grow instead of writing it through an
`(Array *)` cast. The scanner and the parser are the published ones.

Why: the published header's push is undefined behavior under C's aliasing rule,
and GCC 16 at -O2 and -O3 compiles it into a heap overflow on two
`{-# LANGUAGE #-}` pragmas, which aborted the editor (E7e shipped it, E7g
unshipped it). E7h restored the grammar on `.cargo/config.toml`'s
`-fno-strict-aliasing`, which holds for every compiler measured but reaches only
builds cargo starts at the repository root: E7h review 1 built pmacs with
`cargo install --git` and it aborted on the first keystroke into the pragma
file in seven of nine runs. The owner ruled at E7h's fix round 1 that the
conforming header is vendored, so the fix travels with the source; the flag
stays for every other grammar's C and the runtime's. Held by
`tests/e7g_review1_serialization_witnesses.rs` (this copy, not crates.io) and
`tests/e7g_review1_probes.rs` (no shipped scanner on the old header).

To drop this copy: a crates.io release generated by tree-sitter's CLI 0.24 or
later (its `src/tree_sitter/array.h` passing no `(Array *)` to `_array__grow`),
fuzzed clean with `scripts/fuzz-grammars --grammar haskell --seconds 600`, the
`[patch.crates-io]` entry and this directory removed in the same commit. A
newer release still on the old header is carried forward by replacing this
directory with it and this header, never by dropping the patch.
